title: What kind of game hardest to clone now?
author: Free-Version-2746

comments.author: caxco93
comments.body: why would silksong be harder to clone? it is just a metroidvania

replies.author: Free-Version-2746
replies.body: Not seen any metroidvania on this sub yet?

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: You can make a legally distinct Metroid clone in one, four sentence prompt. I've done it.

comments.author: 1shox
comments.body:
AI cant listen to audio, really.

so, games that rely on good audio? or audio mechanics?

replies.author: Equal-Border-7793
replies.body: AI can replicate content; it is capable of generating beatmaps simply by analyzing audio. The real challenge in creating a music game lies in having excellent music.

replies.author: frogic
replies.body: yue2 is so incredible at song generation I think that problem is mostly solved or soonish solved.

comments.author: Suspicious-Engineer7
comments.body: Any actually decent game is hard to clone, because cloned games have such shallow content it's not even funny. You can get the mechanics kind of there, but good luck having any charm without putting in the work.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
Depends on what you're trying to clone. Genre and mechanics? Can pretty much do any of them. Look, feel, and playability? MMO. Large, intricate open world games (Skyrim). Anything "unique" that wouldn't be well represented in training data.

Silksong is an action platformer. There's ten thousand of those. Not a difficult clone.

comments.author: Hisagi10
comments.body: the beggier the game the harder to clone

comments.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
comments.body: Games with a lot of different animations

comments.author: Equal-Border-7793
comments.body: As for those high-quality 3D games, given the current pace of large model evolution, it will likely be possible to replicate them directly by next year. Regarding decompilation, many 3D games have already been successfully decompiled.

comments.author: BeaveItToLeever
comments.body:
No straight clone ever hits the mark, so maybe all of them.

Though speaking purely of just the amount of work? Probably something like Smash Ultimate. The amount of animations alone should take the wind out of the sails of anyone.

comments.author: Ink_code
comments.body: If by clone we are saying distinct enough but same idea,then a game where story is a main focus, so RPGs, the default in creative writing for models feels weird and they are also very safety maxxed so dialogue feels unnatural and it also takes quite a lot of effort wrangling them to get them to spit out a somewhat decent story chapter.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body:
Games with a lot of cinematic scenes,  AAA games with gorgeous effects, games that require a lot of gameplay tuning with really deep systems where a lot of QA and technical system simulation would be necessary to balance gameplay, progression, and balance in game economy. 

So in my opinion, I don’t think Silksong is that game. It’s AA indie Metroidvania in 2D.

comments.author: pazh1
comments.body:
Imho any good, genuinely fun game is basically impossible to clone with LLMs right now.  
LLMs can copy mechanics, systems and visuals, but they at the end they have no real concept of fun.   
That’s why we see 99% of vibe-cloned games end up being technically impressive for someone with no game design, coding skills, but ultimately just soulless junk.  
You can clone the ingredients easily now. You can’t clone the design judgment that made the original good.

comments.author: Angsty-Teen-0810
comments.body: Any 3d game with extremely detailed specific animations (FromSoftware games)
